facts.fact: The Databricks product name changes page lists 'Data + AI Platform' as the current name, with 'Databricks Data Intelligence Platform' and 'Data Intelligence Platform' as former names (page last updated 2026-11-10; no rename date given) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/product-name-changes)
'Databricks Lakehouse Platform' is also listed as a former name of the Databricks 'Data + AI Platform' (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/product-name-changes)
'Data + AI Platform' is the current name of the Databricks platform (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/product-name-changes)

A Databricks account contains one or more workspaces managed from the account console; with Unity Catalog enabled, users, groups and service principals are managed at the account level and account admins assign them to workspaces (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)
Only Databricks account admins create workspaces (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)

The account admin who creates a Databricks workspace becomes its workspace admin automatically; other account admins have no workspace access by default but can grant themselves or others the workspace admin role on any workspace in the account (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)

Databricks accounts created after 2023-11-08 (AWS) or 2023-11-09 (Azure) might have Unity Catalog enabled by default, with an auto-created metastore per region (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)

Identity federation is on by default for all new Databricks workspaces since 2026-06-09, including those not attached to a Unity Catalog metastore; existing workspaces are not affected (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/june)

The Databricks on AWS Standard tier is end-of-life; remaining Standard tier workspaces were automatically upgraded to Premium on 2025-10-01 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)
Databricks on AWS has two platform tiers, Premium and Enterprise, and new accounts start on Premium (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)
Databricks account admins upgrade to the Enterprise tier from account console Settings (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)
Databricks pricing pages state that Azure Databricks' Premium tier corresponds to the Enterprise tier on AWS and GCP (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/model-serving)

An AWS Marketplace account can be the payment method for a Databricks account; several Marketplace accounts can link to one Databricks account, but each Marketplace account links to only one Databricks account (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)
Cancelling Databricks in AWS Marketplace only removes the payment method; contract accounts go through the Databricks account team (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)

Databricks on AWS Marketplace offers a 14-day free trial with up to $400 in trial credits, then pay-as-you-go metered in Databricks Consumption Units (shown 2026-11-14), with private offers for custom pricing from Databricks sales (secondary) (https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-wtyi5lgtce6n6)
Databricks is listed on AWS Marketplace with a free trial, pay-as-you-go and private offers (secondary) (https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-wtyi5lgtce6n6)

Databricks Free Edition accounts cannot be upgraded to the full platform; Free Edition users must create a new account through the Databricks Free Trial sign-up (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)
Databricks Free Edition accounts cannot be upgraded to the full platform (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/account)

On Azure, creating the first Azure Databricks workspace in an Entra ID tenant creates the Databricks account, and a Microsoft Entra ID Global Administrator must establish the first account admin by signing in at `https://accounts.azuredatabricks.net` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)
The Azure Databricks account console is not available in Azure Government regions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)

Creating an Azure Databricks workspace requires the Azure RBAC Contributor or Owner role at subscription level, or a custom role (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)

A custom role for creating Azure Databricks workspaces needs `Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces/*`, `Microsoft.Databricks/accessConnectors/*`, resource group read/write and deployment permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)
Azure Contributor or Owner on the subscription also grants Azure Databricks workspace admin on first login (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)
Azure Contributor on the subscription grants Azure Databricks workspace admin on first login (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)

Day-one asks for an engineer joining a Databricks engagement: workspace URL and account ID; a user assigned to the workspace with needed entitlements; a dedicated service principal for the agent with OAuth secret or workload identity federation policy; `USE CATALOG`/`USE SCHEMA`/`SELECT`/`EXECUTE` grants on the target catalog and schema; `CAN USE` on a SQL warehouse; `CAN QUERY` on serving endpoints or `EXECUTE` on Unity Gateway model services; whether user authorization (OBO) is enabled; and the network policy/ingress rules in force (synthesis of sources in sections 2-4) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

Ask for a dedicated Databricks service principal for the agent with an OAuth secret or a workload identity federation policy (synthesis) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

facts.fact: Databricks account-level SSO supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC with unified login (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/single-sign-on/)
Databricks account-level SSO supports OIDC as well as SAML 2.0 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/single-sign-on/)

With account-level SSO enabled, all users including admins sign in via SSO, and up to 20 emergency access users can use username, password and security key (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/single-sign-on/)
Unified login is mandatory for Databricks accounts created after 2023-06-21 or that had not configured SSO before 2024-12-12 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/single-sign-on/)

Databricks recommends automatic identity management over SCIM for syncing users and groups; SCIM provisioning is the fallback when the IdP does not support automatic identity management (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/single-sign-on/)

JIT provisioning creates Databricks users on first login, and supported IdPs include Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, OneLogin, AWS IAM Identity Center, Keycloak and JumpCloud (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/single-sign-on/)

Automatic identity management with Microsoft Entra ID is GA since 2026-05-26 and syncs users, service principals and groups from Entra ID without SCIM (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/may)

Automatic identity management with Okta is GA since 2026-07-03 (Public Preview began 2026-06-09), with Okta as the source of truth for group memberships (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/june)

The account access denylist for automatic identity management is in Public Preview since 2026-05-22 (AWS and GCP); denying a group blocks its members (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/may)
Account admins use the account access denylist to block users, groups or service principals from the Databricks account (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/may)

Databricks SCIM provisioning cannot sync service principals; Entra ID service principals sync via automatic identity management (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/users-groups/service-principals)

A Databricks service principal is an API-only identity for automation; account admins add service principals to the account and assign them to workspaces, workspace admins can also add them, and the creator becomes a service principal manager (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/users-groups/service-principals)
Account admins add Databricks service principals to the account and assign them to workspaces (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/users-groups/service-principals)

The `Service principal manager` role manages roles on the service principal, and account admins hold it on all service principals (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/users-groups/service-principals)
The `Service principal user` role lets someone run jobs as the service principal and is not inherited by managers (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/users-groups/service-principals)

Databricks workspace admins can create tokens for a service principal only if they also hold the `Service principal user` role (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/users-groups/service-principals)
The Databricks auth overview lists OAuth token federation (recommended), OAuth M2M for service principals and OAuth U2M for users (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/)
Databricks PATs are labelled legacy in the auth docs (as of 2026-11-14) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/pat)
Databricks service principals authenticate with OAuth M2M (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/)
OAuth U2M is the Databricks OAuth flow for users (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/)

Databricks unified authentication uses `DATABRICKS_HOST`, `DATABRICKS_ACCOUNT_ID`, `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID` and `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET`, and Databricks recommends a configuration profile in `.databrickscfg` instead of manually set environment variables (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/)
Databricks OAuth M2M access tokens last one hour (`expires_in: 3600`) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-m2m)

The Databricks workspace token endpoint is `https://<databricks-instance>/oidc/v1/token`, the account endpoint is `https://accounts.cloud.databricks.com/oidc/accounts/<account-id>/v1/token`, and the grant is `grant_type=client_credentials&scope=all-apis` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-m2m)

A Databricks service principal can have at most five OAuth secrets, each valid up to 730 days; account admins and workspace admins can create secrets (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-m2m)
A Databricks OAuth secret is shown only once, and a secret without scopes gets `all-apis` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-m2m)

Unused Databricks service principal OAuth secrets are auto-deleted after 90 days since 2026-09-16 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-m2m)

Databricks service principal OAuth secrets can be restricted to API scopes such as `sql`, `jobs` or `unity-catalog` since 2026-08-29 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
OAuth secret scopes cannot be changed after generation, and a secret with the `authentication` scope can create tokens with any scope (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-m2m)

facts.fact: OAuth device code flow for headless machines is in Beta since 2026-10-30; it issues a workspace-level OAuth token after browser sign-in on another device, and admins enable it on the Previews page (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

OAuth custom identity claims (announced 2026-10-19) let one Databricks service principal filter data per end user: a custom claim added to the service principal's OAuth token can drive row filtering (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

facts.source: Databricks default OAuth apps for external AI agents
facts.fact: Default OAuth apps for external AI agents are GA since 2026-10-27: ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code and Cursor connect with default OAuth client IDs, so an account admin does not need to create an OAuth app (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

facts.source: Databricks default OAuth apps for external AI agents
facts.fact: ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code and Cursor connect to Databricks MCP servers through default OAuth apps (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Databricks OAuth token federation has two forms: account-wide token federation lets all users and service principals exchange IdP JWTs for Databricks OAuth tokens, and workload identity federation lets an external workload authenticate as a specific service principal (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-federation)

Workload identity federation is a form of Databricks OAuth token federation in which an external workload authenticates as a specific Databricks service principal via a federation policy, with no Databricks secret (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-federation)

Databricks workload identity federation supports GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI/CD, CircleCI, AWS IAM workloads, Jenkins, Terraform Cloud and Bitbucket Pipelines (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/oauth-federation-provider)

GitHub Actions federation to Databricks uses issuer `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` and `DATABRICKS_AUTH_TYPE=github-oidc`, needs `id-token: write`, `DATABRICKS_HOST` and `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID`, and the audience defaults to the account ID (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/provider-github)
Create a GitHub Actions federation policy with `databricks account service-principal-federation-policy create <SP_NUMERIC_ID>` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/provider-github)

GitHub repos created, renamed or transferred on or after 2026-07-15 use numeric-ID subjects such as `repo:org@123/repo@456:environment:prod` in Databricks federation policies (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/provider-github)

Databricks PATs are scoped to one workspace and cannot automate account-level APIs; a user can create up to 600 PATs per workspace, and PATs unused for 90 days are revoked automatically (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/pat)

New Databricks PATs default to a 730-day maximum lifetime set by `maxTokenLifetimeDays`; Databricks recommends lifetimes under 90 days, the setting applies only to new tokens, and users get expiry email about seven days ahead (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/access-control/tokens)

Databricks workspace admins can disable PAT authentication per workspace (PATs are enabled by default); disabling blocks PAT auth and creation but does not delete tokens, and account admins can review and revoke tokens in the account console Token report (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/access-control/tokens)
Managing Databricks PATs requires Premium or above (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/access-control/tokens)
Partner Connect and some partner integrations need PATs, so disabling PAT authentication can break them (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/access-control/tokens)

`POST /api/2.0/token/create` accepts a `scopes` array (empty array means full access; literal `all-apis` is rejected) and `autoscope_enabled`; list scopes with `GET /api/2.0/token-scopes` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/pat)
Databricks PATs support API scopes and (Preview) auto-scoping, which narrows a token to observed APIs after 30 days and is a workspace preview (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/pat)

Expiring service principal token emails are GA since 2026-07-22: workspace admins are emailed when a service principal token with a lifetime over seven days, used at least once, expires within seven days (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july)
Databricks has no separate 'agent identity' type; an agent's runtime identity is a Databricks service principal (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

On Databricks Apps, each app gets a dedicated, non-shareable service principal that is deleted with the app, and its credentials are injected as `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID` and `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/auth)

Databricks recommends deploying new agents on Databricks Apps rather than Model Serving, because Apps give full control over code, server configuration and deployment and support more OBO scopes (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)

Agents on Databricks Apps use 'App authorization' (default, formerly called service principal auth), which can be combined with User authorization in one agent (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

Agents on Databricks Apps can use 'User authorization' (Public Preview, formerly on-behalf-of-user (OBO)), which receives the downscoped user token in the `x-forwarded-access-token` header (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)
Databricks Apps User authorization must be enabled by a workspace admin (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

facts.fact: Databricks Apps user authorization requires declared scopes in `user_api_scopes` such as `sql`, `genie`, `files`, `model-serving` and `ai-gateway`; defaults are `iam.access-control:read` and `iam.current-user:read` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/auth ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

Workspace admins control the Apps user scope allowlist via `allowedAppsUserApiScopes` (default `*`; an empty array disables user authorization) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/auth)
Apps user scope changes take up to 5 minutes, and existing apps must restart after user authorization is first enabled (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/auth)

Agents on Model Serving use automatic authentication passthrough, on-behalf-of-user (Public Preview) or manual credentials; passthrough runs with the deployer's permissions using short-lived credentials for resources declared via the `resources` parameter of `log_model()`, and Databricks recommends it where possible (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)
Manual auth on Model Serving passes long-lived credentials through environment variables (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)

Model Serving OBO is disabled by default, needs a workspace admin to enable it, and requires MLflow 2.22.1 or later; declare scopes with MLflow `AuthPolicy`/`UserAuthPolicy(api_scopes=[...])` (e.g. `model-serving`, `ai-search`) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)

With Model Serving OBO, create clients inside `predict` with `WorkspaceClient(credentials_strategy=ModelServingUserCredentials())` from `databricks_ai_bridge` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)
Model Serving OBO does not support UC Volumes (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)

Lakebase Postgres accepts a one-hour Databricks OAuth token as the Postgres password; tokens are workspace-scoped and need SSL, and each identity needs a Postgres role created with the `databricks_auth` extension (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/oltp/projects/authentication)
Generate a Lakebase Postgres credential with the CLI `generate-database-credential` (or the SDKs) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/oltp/projects/authentication)
Native Postgres password auth is off by default for new Lakebase projects, and the PgBouncer pooler does not support OAuth (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/oltp/projects/authentication)

Databricks admin roles are `Account admin`, `Workspace admin`, `Metastore admin`, `Marketplace admin` and `Billing admin`; account admin manages workspaces, cloud resources, identities, settings and subscriptions (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)
The Databricks workspace admin manages one workspace's identities and compute (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)
The Databricks metastore admin manages privileges and ownership in a Unity Catalog metastore (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)
The Databricks marketplace admin manages the Marketplace provider profile (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)
The Databricks billing admin views budgets and manages serverless usage policies (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/admin-concepts)

Databricks workspace admins are members of the reserved `admins` system group, and in identity-federated workspaces a directly assigned group can be added to `admins` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/admin/admin-concepts)

The Unity Catalog metastore admin role is optional for workspaces created after 2023-11-08 and auto-enabled metastores have none; workspace admins get metastore-level create privileges via system group `_workspace_admins_<workspace_name>_<workspace_id>` and own the workspace catalog, but a metastore admin is still needed to change ownership of objects you don't own (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/admin-privileges)
Databricks recommends assigning the metastore admin role to a group (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/admin-privileges)

The Unity Catalog securable hierarchy is metastore > catalog > schema > objects; schema objects include tables, views, materialized views, volumes, functions, models, features, flows and secrets, while external locations, storage/service credentials, connections, services, shares and clean rooms sit outside the schema tree (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)

Reading a Unity Catalog table requires `SELECT` on the table plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` on its parents; `SELECT` can be inherited from a schema or catalog grant (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)
`USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` grant no data access by themselves (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)

Calling a Unity Catalog function or registered model requires `EXECUTE` plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA`; models are a type of function, and `EXECUTE` on a model also allows viewing version metadata and downloading model files (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)

Other Unity Catalog privileges relevant to agents include `READ VOLUME`, `WRITE VOLUME`, `USE CONNECTION`, `ACCESS` (service credentials), `BROWSE`, `READ METADATA`, `CREATE SERVICE`, `CREATE SECRET`, `MANAGE` and `MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL`; fine-grained `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` are Beta and `EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA` is Preview (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)

Unity Catalog `ALL PRIVILEGES` excludes `MANAGE`, `READ METADATA`, `EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA` and `EXTERNAL USE LOCATION` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-governance/unity-catalog/manage-privileges/privileges)

facts.fact: Unity Catalog secrets support `BROWSE` and up to 1,000 secrets per schema (announced 2026-11-02); `BROWSE` on a catalog exposes secret metadata without values (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

Databricks permission levels: serving endpoints `CAN VIEW`, `CAN QUERY`, `CAN MANAGE`; SQL warehouses `CAN VIEW`, `CAN MONITOR`, `CAN USE`, `IS OWNER`, `CAN MANAGE`; Genie Agents `CAN VIEW`, `CAN RUN`, `CAN EDIT`, `CAN MANAGE` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/access-control/)

Databricks permission levels: jobs `CAN VIEW`, `CAN MANAGE RUN`, `IS OWNER`, `CAN MANAGE`; secret scopes `READ`, `WRITE`, `MANAGE`; AI Search endpoints and Lakebase projects `CAN CREATE`, `CAN USE`, `CAN MANAGE` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/access-control/)
Databricks Apps permissions are `CAN USE` and `CAN MANAGE`, and `CAN MANAGE` is needed to edit app settings and scopes (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/auth)

Least-privilege grants for an agent on Databricks Apps (app authorization): SQL warehouse `Can Use`; Model Serving endpoint `Can Query`; UC function `Can Execute`; Genie Agent `Can Run`; AI Search index `Can Select`; UC table `SELECT`; UC connection `Use Connection`; UC volume `Can Read`/`Can Read and Write`; Lakebase `Can Connect and Create`; MLflow experiment `Can Edit`; use a dedicated service principal per app (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

Automatic authentication passthrough on Model Serving supports declared resources with minimum MLflow versions: SQL warehouse `Use Endpoint` (2.16.1), serving endpoint `Can Query` (2.13.1), UC function `EXECUTE` (2.16.1), Genie Agent `Can Run` (2.17.1), AI Search index `Can Use` (2.13.1), UC table `SELECT` (2.18.0), UC connection `Use Connection` (2.17.1), Lakebase `databricks_superuser` (3.3.2) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)
Automatic authentication passthrough is not supported for Unity Gateway model services (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/model-serving/agent-authentication-model-serving)

Granting an agent a Genie Agent also requires access to the Genie Agent's underlying tables, SQL warehouses and UC functions; workspace MCP endpoints need access to every index and function in the referenced schemas, and MCP Services need `EXECUTE` plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)
Querying a Unity Gateway model service requires `EXECUTE` on the service plus `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/govern-model-services)

All account users have `EXECUTE` on `system.ai` by default; restrict access by revoking the account users group's schema-level grant on `system.ai` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/govern-model-services)

Unity Gateway model service queries are evaluated against the service owner's privileges, so the owner must keep `EXECUTE` on every destination including fallbacks (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/govern-model-services)
Managing `system.ai` needs metastore admin or `MANAGE` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/govern-model-services)

Databricks workspace entitlements are `workspace-consume`, `workspace-access`, `databricks-sql-access`, `allow-cluster-create` and `allow-instance-pool-create` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/entitlements)

Consumer access lets a user view shared dashboards, Genie Agents and Apps, query Unity Gateway services and query SQL warehouses from BI tools, but not create Unity Gateway assets (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/entitlements)

From 2026-06-15 the Databricks `users` group is being changed to carry no entitlements; new principals receive only the entitlements selected when added instead of inheriting `workspace-access` and `databricks-sql-access` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/entitlements)

Consumer access to query Unity Gateway services is GA since 2026-10-15; users with the consumer access entitlement no longer need an account admin to enable a preview, and admins can apply budgets and rate limits (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Databricks RBAC (assumable roles) is GA since 2026-08-19 (Public Preview began 2026-07-22); a role is a group with the `Assume` permission, and while acting as a role only the role's permissions apply; audit logs record `run_by` and `run_as` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/rbac/)
An account admin enables Databricks RBAC for the account, then workspace admins enable it per workspace (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/rbac/)

A Databricks service principal or agent can get a role-scoped OAuth token by adding `assume_group=<group-id>` to the workspace token request; both the service principal and role must be assigned to the workspace, and users can pick a role at `databricks auth login` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/rbac/switch-roles)
Account-level token requests do not support Databricks role assumption (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/auth/rbac/switch-roles)

facts.fact: ABAC policies can check the calling OAuth application and whether a request is on behalf of a user (Beta, 2026-08-21), which can restrict what an agent reads on a user's behalf (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
Identity attributes from the IdP for ABAC column masks are Beta since 2026-08-13 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
ABAC DENY policies cover AI securables (model, MCP, agent and skill services) in Beta since 2026-11-12 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)
Serverless usage policies were formerly called serverless budget policies (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/product-name-changes)

Serverless usage policies tag serverless usage for cost attribution, with tags landing in `custom_tags` of `system.billing.usage`; they cover notebooks, jobs, Lakeflow pipelines, model serving, Lakebase Autoscaling and Apps, and permissions are `User` and `Manager` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/usage/budget-policies)
Workspace admins create serverless usage policies (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/usage/budget-policies)
An account-wide view of serverless usage policies needs `Billing admin` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/usage/budget-policies)

Budget access can be delegated with the `Budget Manager` and `Budget Viewer` roles (announced 2026-10-16), which account and workspace admins grant to users, groups or service principals (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
The `Budget Viewer` role (announced 2026-10-16) delegates view access to Databricks budgets (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
AI Gateway is now named Unity Gateway; former names are AI Gateway, Unity AI Gateway and Mosaic AI Gateway (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/product-name-changes)
Unity Gateway is GA since 2026-08-04, while service policies and agent services remain Beta (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
Unity Gateway governs models, agents, MCP servers and tools as Unity Catalog securables (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/)

Unity Gateway features: rate limits, traffic splitting, fallbacks, Smart Routing, per-user budgets, service policies (guardrails), MCP tool filtering (built-in `system.ai.github_policy`), usage tracking and inference tables (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/)

Unity Gateway fronts Foundation Model APIs in `system.ai`, BYOK external providers, custom model services, MCP tools, UC functions and HTTP connections (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/)

The Unity Gateway API and developer tools are GA since 2026-09-16; the API manages model services, model provider services and MCP services via Terraform, CLI and SDKs (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)
The `ug` CLI for coding agents shipped 2026-09-22 and connects Claude Code, Codex and similar tools to Unity Gateway (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)

Unity Gateway guardrails include partner guardrails via external service policies (Beta, 2026-10-07) and a Jailbreak guardrail for MCP tool calls (Beta, 2026-10-21); custom service policies can require request tags (Beta, 2026-10-09) and can be written in Python (Beta, 2026-11-11, select regions) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

Legacy AI Gateway guardrails on serving endpoints use Llama Guard for safety and Presidio for PII (unverified against the current Unity Gateway docs) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/configure-ai-gateway-endpoints)

Older docs state legacy AI Gateway output guardrails are not supported for embeddings or streaming, guardrails/fallbacks are not supported on custom model endpoints, and up to 20 rate limits (5 group-specific) per endpoint as QPM/TPM (unverified against the current Unity Gateway docs) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/configure-ai-gateway-endpoints)

Unity Gateway usage is recorded in `system.ai_gateway.usage` (Public Preview; request/response details, tokens, latency and routing) and `system.ai_gateway.external_model_spend` (Beta; estimated external model spend); `system.serving.endpoint_usage` and `system.serving.served_entities` (Public Preview) cover serving endpoints; default retention is 395 days (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/)

Databricks audit logs are in `system.access.audit` (Public Preview, 395-day retention); billing data is in `system.billing.usage` and `system.billing.list_prices` (indefinite retention) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/)

Access to Databricks system tables requires account admin plus metastore admin by default, or grants of `USE CATALOG` on `system` and `USE SCHEMA`/`SELECT` on the schemas (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/)
Configurable system table retention of 30-3,650 days is Beta via `st_retention` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/)
Unity Gateway skill usage (list, load, file fetch) is recorded in audit logs since 2026-10-30 (Beta) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Databricks serverless egress control uses account-level network policies in Full Access or Restricted Access mode (one policy per workspace); Restricted Access allows UC external locations, listed FQDNs and S3 buckets and same-workspace APIs, supports dry-run mode, and covers notebooks, jobs, SQL warehouses, Lakeflow pipelines, Model Serving and Databricks Apps (limited) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/serverless-network-security/network-policies)
Databricks serverless network policies require the Enterprise tier (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/serverless-network-security/network-policies)

Under Restricted Access network policies, external model providers and MCP servers must be added as allowed destinations (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/serverless-network-security/network-policies)

facts.fact: Blocking specific internet destinations in Databricks network policies is in Public Preview since 2026-06-23; blocks apply via the network policies REST API regardless of access mode (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/june)

Databricks context-based ingress control is GA since 2026-07-21; account-level policies and cross-workspace access are Beta (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/front-end/context-based-ingress ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july)

Account admins write ingress allow/deny rules combining identity, request type (workspace UI, API, Apps runtime, Lakebase runtime), source IP, private endpoints and partner platforms (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/front-end/context-based-ingress)
Context-based ingress control requires the Enterprise tier, and IP access lists are ANDed with ingress policies (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/front-end/context-based-ingress)

ChatGPT and Claude can be allowed as partner platforms in context-based ingress policies (announced 2026-11-10); Databricks maintains their IP ranges so hosted MCP clients can be allowed without tracking IPs (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

Databricks network connectivity configurations (NCCs) are account-level regional objects that manage serverless private endpoints; account admins create NCCs and attach them to workspaces in a region (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/serverless-network-security/)
Databricks serverless private endpoints are charged per hour and per GB processed (as of 2026-11-14) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/serverless-network-security/)
The legacy Databricks serverless stable IP list was decommissioned (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/serverless-network-security/)

Private connectivity for Databricks on AWS uses front-end and back-end AWS PrivateLink, customer-managed VPC and serverless private connectivity; Private Link for account-level resources is Beta since 2026-07-06 and private network gateway is Private Preview since 2026-08-24 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/network/ ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
Serverless private connectivity to AWS-managed resources (e.g. S3) is GA since 2026-10-12 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Private connectivity on Azure Databricks uses front-end and back-end Azure Private Link, VNet injection, secure cluster connectivity and serverless private endpoints via NCC; serverless can reach Azure Storage, SQL Database and VNet resources through private endpoint rules (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/security/network/)
Private connectivity for Databricks on GCP uses Private Service Connect (front-end and back-end) and customer-managed VPC (https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/en/security/network/)

Since 2026-10-26 account-level security features (private connectivity, ingress/egress controls and encryption) are available by default at GA without a Previews page step, but account admins must still configure them (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Databricks Geos and Designated Services control data residency for managed AI features; account admins set 'Enforce data processing within workspace Geography for Designated Services' per workspace under Security and compliance, and cross-Geo processing is on by default for workspaces outside the US and EU without a compliance security profile (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/databricks-geos)
Foundation Model APIs is a Databricks Designated Service that uses Databricks Geos for data residency (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-models/)
Some Foundation Model APIs pay-per-token models carry a 10% price uplift when regional processing is enabled (as of 2026-11-14) (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/foundation-model-serving)
Genie agentic capabilities are processed within India for India-region workspaces since 2026-10-14 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Databricks does not train models offered to others on data submitted to its AI-assistive features, and model partners do not retain that data, even for abuse monitoring (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/databricksiq/databricksiq-trust)

The 'partner-powered AI features' setting switches Databricks AI-assistive features between partner models (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI on Databricks, Anthropic on Databricks) and Databricks-hosted models (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/databricksiq/databricksiq-trust)

Compliance security profile standards include C5, CCCS Medium, DoD IL5, FedRAMP Class C and D, HIPAA, HITRUST, IRAP, ISMAP, K-FSI, PCI-DSS, TISAX and UK Cyber Essentials Plus; HIPAA requires a BAA (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/privacy/security-profile)
Enabling the compliance security profile incurs the Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/security/privacy/security-profile)
Unity Gateway supports all compliance security profile standards since 2026-09-17 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)
Databricks Apps is on by default for compliance-profile workspaces since 2026-09-18 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)

facts.fact: Databricks bills consumption in Databricks Units (DBUs) at per-second granularity, pay-as-you-go or under committed-use contracts; prices vary by cloud, region and tier, and storage and networking are billed separately (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing)
Azure Databricks is billed through the Azure subscription (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing)

Foundation Model APIs bill pay-per-token as DBUs per million tokens; shown 2026-11-14: example SKU price $0.07/DBU (AWS us-east-1), e.g. Llama 3.3 70B 7.143 input / 21.429 output DBU per 1M tokens (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/foundation-model-serving)

Foundation Model APIs provisioned throughput is billed in DBU per hour per 50 model units with on-demand, 1-month and 3-month reservations, and the priority pay-per-token tier is requested with `service_tier: "priority"` (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/foundation-model-serving ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-models/)

Model Serving GPU endpoints bill DBUs per hour by GPU type; shown 2026-11-14: A10G 1 GPU 20.00 DBU/h, H100 1 GPU 100.00 DBU/h, H100 8 GPU 800.00 DBU/h (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing/model-serving)

Databricks Apps bill DBUs per hour by compute size: Medium (2 vCPU, 6 GB) 0.5 DBU/h default; Large (4 vCPU, 12 GB) 1 DBU/h; XLarge (12 vCPU, 48 GB) 3 DBU/h in some regions (as of 2026-11-14) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/compute-size)

Genie Agents, Genie Code and Genie One moved to pay-as-you-go DBU billing on 2026-07-08; users get 150 free DBUs of LLM usage per month, and user usage of Genie One and Genie Agents is free through 2027-01-31 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie/)
Service principal usage of Genie is excluded from the free-usage promotion through 2027-01-31 and is billed (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
Genie Code usage above 150 DBUs per month gets a 25% discount through 2027-01-31 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie/)
Genie One moved to pay-as-you-go DBU billing on 2026-07-08, and user usage is free through 2027-01-31 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july)

Databricks budgets are GA since 2026-07-06, including Unity Gateway budgets with per-user thresholds and blocking; AI Functions usage counts toward Unity Gateway budgets since 2026-11-01, and budget alert webhooks are Beta since 2026-11-10 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

External provider spend (Amazon Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry) can be tracked and capped since 2026-08-28 via 'External Model Spend in Budgets' (Beta) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
A Databricks Spend Status API shipped 2026-10-26 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

Unity Gateway can apply a price multiplier to external model spend estimates (announced 2026-09-19) to reflect negotiated provider rates, for model provider services only (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)

Undiscounted per-SKU Databricks list prices are published in the Databricks Price List and in `system.billing.list_prices` (https://www.databricks.com/product/pricing ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/)
`system.billing.list_prices` holds undiscounted per-SKU Databricks list prices (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/system-tables/)
